title: Interfaces
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of interfaces using at least one correct term from the lesson.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Interfaces** as part of **Inheritance, Interfaces, and Polymorphism**. Use interfaces and inheritance when they express substitutability, and prefer composition when an object should contain or coordinate collaborators. Use the subtopics—Declaring Interfaces, Interface Properties and Default Implementations, Implementing Multiple Interfaces—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: These concepts help you model domain rules and reusable APIs. Good boundaries reduce accidental mutation, unsafe casts, and code that is difficult to extend.

items.text: Declaring Interfaces should support a clear object invariant: make valid states easy to represent, restrict mutation to the intended API, and keep initialization and dependencies explicit.
